newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Expiring Australia 10-yr bond ending with a sprint.
newsitem.headline: Expiring Australia 10-yr bond ending with a sprint.

text.p: Australian bonds got off to a brisk start to the week with 10-year bond yields at their lowest level since February 1994 at below 7.0 percent, and extending the rally seen in Friday's SYCOM session.

The market, already extremely bullish over the possibility of a further local monetary policy easing, received a further boost on Friday after U.S. Treasuries rallied on a weaker than expected U.S. PPI for May.
Final rollover activity to September from June three- and 10-year bond futures contracts ahead of the midday expiries bolstered the early trade.

The June 10-year bond contract overcame the 93.015 December 1996 peak as the local market chased the U.S. rally in SYCOM trade with the recent U.S. data flow seen lessening the chance of a tightening by the Federal Reserve when the Federal Open Market Committee meets on July 1 and 2.
Locally, the market remains on full alert for a policy easing after last week's extremely weak labour force data, along with the spate of other soft indicators.
The market is fully prepared for an easing at any time given the surprise timing of the last official rate cut to 5.5 percent on May 23. The Reserve Bank board meets on July 1.

The local market generally outperformed the dollar bloc with the Australian/U.S. 10-year spread retesting the low seen last week, a level not seen for more than three years. The short end of the Canadian curve outperformed slightly on lessening concerns of a U.S. tightening.
